page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge is an entry-level, budget-oriented virtual server belonging to the ecs.e family. It features 4 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, backed by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, which translates to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge demonstrates limited performance capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10%, reflecting its shared CPU allocation and low resource density. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show poor throughput, with bzip3 decompression and Passmark encryption tests scoring in the lowest decile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is positioned as a highly economical option for workloads that do not require sustained or high-performance compute resources. The shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage or high-speed networking make it a low-cost entry point. Tradeoffs include potential resource contention due to the shared CPU model and low overall memory bandwidth.

The ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge is best suited for low-intensity workloads. Appropriate use cases include development and testing environments, lightweight background tasks, basic static web serving, and small-scale database operations with minimal concurrent traffic.
